title: Symphony No. 5 in E-flat major
hook: A symphony that grows from a soft horn call into a hymn inspired by sixteen swans in flight.

painting.title: Mute Swans in Evening Flight
painting.pairingNote: Swans flying low over a northern marsh at dusk, painted by Sibelius’s Swedish contemporary; the finale was inspired by sixteen swans Sibelius watched in flight.

facts: The symphony was written for Sibelius’s 50th birthday, 8 December 1915, which Finland marked as a national holiday. He conducted the first performance that evening in Helsinki.
He was not satisfied. He revised it in 1916 and again from 1917 to 1919, joining the first two of its four movements into one. The version heard today is the last, first played on 24 November 1919.
In April 1915, while he was working on it, he saw sixteen swans flying by and called it one of the great experiences of his life. The swinging horn theme of the finale grew from that moment.

There are no big tunes at the start. Short fragments, first heard in the horns and woodwinds, slowly join up into larger shapes. It is the only one of Sibelius’s symphonies with every movement in a major key.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a slow horn call that speeds up into a whirling dance (I), a light, plucked intermezzo (II), rushing strings and the great swan hymn (III).

movements.heading: Tempo molto moderato – Allegro moderato – Presto
movements.tempo: Tempo molto moderato – Allegro moderato – Presto
movements.summary: Two movements in one. It begins slowly, with a soft horn call and woodwinds fluttering around it, sinks into a dark passage for bassoon, then rises to a broad climax. Without any break the music then turns into a quick dance and keeps accelerating to the end.

mainIdeas.name: The horn call
mainIdeas.description: a soft, rising phrase of a few notes. Much of the symphony grows out of it.

mainIdeas.name: The woodwind pairs
mainIdeas.description: woodwinds fluttering in twos, like birds answering the horn.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a light, quick tune in three, which takes over in the second half.

stops.hear: A soft horn call, with other horns holding long notes beneath; the woodwinds answer with fluttering pairs of notes
stops.happening: The opening idea. Almost everything that follows is built from it

stops.hear: A short, lilting woodwind figure over trembling strings, then a quiet, hymn-like phrase in horns and woodwinds
stops.happening: More fragments are added, each only a few notes long

stops.hear: The horn call returns, now over a shimmering string [[tremolo|tremolo]]
stops.happening: The ideas go round a second time, changed

stops.hear: A bassoon plays a slow, mournful line on its own while the strings murmur and slide underneath
stops.happening: The darkest place in the symphony: the [[development|development]]

stops.hear: The music brightens and broadens; trumpets ring out the horn call
stops.happening: The climax of the slow part, *Largamente*

stops.hear: With no pause, the music lightens into a quick dance in three
stops.happening: *Allegro moderato*: the slow movement has turned into a [[scherzo|scherzo]]

stops.hear: A trumpet plays a jaunty tune over the drums
stops.happening: A contrasting middle section, built from the same material

stops.label: Last 2 minutes
stops.hear: Faster and faster; the whole orchestra races to a blaze of E-flat major
stops.happening: *Presto*: the [[coda|coda]]

notice: Try to catch the moment when the slow music becomes fast. Sibelius speeds up so gradually that the join is very hard to hear.
Compare the horn call at the start with the trumpets at the climax. It is the same idea, grown from a whisper into a proclamation.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Colin Davis recorded the Fifth and Seventh symphonies with the Boston Symphony Orchestra in January 1975, the start of a complete Sibelius cycle in Boston. His opening is broad and patient, so the first movement runs longer than in many recordings. On the Spotify album the symphony is tracks 1–3, followed by the Seventh.

movements.heading: Andante mosso, quasi allegretto
movements.summary: A short, light movement between two large ones. It is a set of [[variation|variation]]s on a very simple tune, first plucked by the strings with the flutes. The variations become busier and faster, then settle back into calm.

mainIdeas.name: The theme
mainIdeas.description: a plain tune of short, detached notes that climb step by step.

stops.hear: Soft, held chords in the woodwinds and horns
stops.happening: A short introduction

stops.hear: Plucked strings and flutes play a simple tune of short notes
stops.happening: The theme, played [[pizzicato|pizzicato]]

stops.hear: The tune again, with woodwinds chirping around it
stops.happening: The first [[variation|variation]]s

stops.hear: The strings take up their bows; the music grows fuller and gradually faster
stops.happening: *Poco a poco stretto*

stops.hear: A calm passage; long, quiet woodwind lines
stops.happening: *Tranquillo*

stops.hear: The pace quickens again and the texture thickens
stops.happening: A second build-up

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The plucked tune comes back at its first speed and the movement closes softly
stops.happening: The theme’s last appearance

notice: Follow the simple plucked tune. It never disappears for long: every variation keeps its outline, even when the rhythm changes around it.

movements.heading: Allegro molto – Largamente assai
movements.summary: The strings rush in like a wind. Then the horns begin a slow, swinging figure, the theme Sibelius linked to the swans. Both ideas come back, and the swinging theme grows into a grand hymn for the whole orchestra. The symphony ends with six chords separated by silence.

mainIdeas.name: The rushing strings
mainIdeas.description: quick, whispering notes passed through the string section.

mainIdeas.name: The swan theme
mainIdeas.description: a slow, swinging figure in the horns, two notes to each swing, with a broad melody sung above it.

stops.hear: Violas, then all the strings, rush in with quick, whispering notes; the woodwinds join
stops.happening: The finale begins

stops.hear: The horns start a slow, swinging figure, like a great bell rocking; above it, woodwinds and strings sing a broad melody
stops.happening: The swan theme. The scholar Donald Tovey compared it to the god Thor swinging his hammer

stops.hear: The rushing strings return, quieter and stranger
stops.happening: *Misterioso*: the opening music comes back, changed

stops.hear: The swinging figure returns, slower and broader, in the brass and then the whole orchestra
stops.happening: The swan theme, now in the home key, E-flat major

stops.hear: The swinging slows almost to a stop; the harmonies grind against each other, then open out
stops.happening: *Largamente assai*: the climax

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: Six loud chords, each followed by a silence
stops.happening: The ending. It was not in the 1915 version; Sibelius added it in his revisions

notice: Count the six final chords and listen to the silences between them. The silences are part of the music.
In the swan theme, keep your ear on the horns. They keep swinging, steady as a pendulum, while the melody above them changes.

threads.title: Pieces of a mosaic
threads.body: Sibelius wrote in his diary that working on this symphony felt like God throwing down pieces of a mosaic for him to fit together. Listen for small fragments that only later join up into tunes.

threads.title: Slow to fast, fast to slow
threads.body: The first movement starts slowly and ends at top speed; the finale starts fast and ends in a broad, slow hymn.

threads.title: Swans
threads.body: The finale’s swinging theme came from sixteen swans in flight, seen in April 1915 while he was writing the first version.

threads.title: Major keys
threads.body: It is Sibelius’s only symphony in which every movement is in a major key. The mood is grand and bright, even in its darkest passages.
